question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sec{\left(\frac{2 x}{y} \right)} + \frac{y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sec{\left(\frac{2 x}{y} \right)} + \frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v + \sec{\left(\frac{2}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v + \sec{\left(\frac{2}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\sec{\left(\frac{2}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\sec{\left(\frac{2}{v} \right)} \\ \left(\frac{1}{\sec{\left(\frac{2}{v} \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =- \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v - \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v - \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{\sin{\left(v \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{x y}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{x y} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} x^{2} + x^{2}}{v x^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} + 1}{v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + \frac{v^{2} + 1}{v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{v} \\ \left(v\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
